newsitem.title: UK: Rolls-Royce to take part in AMR's Boeing deal.
newsitem.headline: Rolls-Royce to take part in AMR's Boeing deal.

text.p: British engineering group Rolls-Royce Plc said on Friday it would supply engines for 12 Boeing 757s to American Airlines as part of the U.S. carrier's huge order for Boeing Co aircraft. Rolls-Royce said AMR Corp's American also reserved purchase rights on a further 38 of the twin-engined airliners. The order will include Rolls-Royce's RB211-535E4B engines, the company said in a statement.
Rolls-Royce said deliveries of the firm 757s was due to be completed during 1998 and 1999.
The company also said its Trent 800 was a "prime candidate" for American's plan to order engines for Boeing 777 jets.

American said on Thursday it ordered 12 Boeing 777s with purchase rights for 38 more as part of a larger deal worth about $6.5 billion that would make Boeing its exclusive provider up to and including 2018.
American's firm 103-'plane order consisted of models ranging from Boeing 737s to 777s.
